title: Unpack the input messages
description:
Window messages pack several values into `wParam` and `lParam`. Write the decoders a window procedure needs. Treat `lParam` as the 64-bit value it is on x64, but only its low 32 bits matter here.

- `mouseX(lParam)` and `mouseY(lParam)`: the low 16 bits and the next 16 bits, each read as a **signed** 16-bit number.
- `repeatCount(lParam)`: bits 0 to 15 of a key message.
- `scanCode(lParam)`: bits 16 to 23.
- `isRepeat(lParam)`: true if bit 30 is set.
- `isKeyUp(lParam)`: true if bit 31 is set.
- `wheelSteps(wParam)`: the high 16 bits of the low 32 bits of `wParam` as a signed number, divided by 120 (one notch of the wheel).

```
mouseX(0x00C80064) = 100,  mouseY(0x00C80064) = 200
mouseX(0x0000FFFF) = -1
repeatCount(0x40150001) = 1, scanCode(...) = 0x15, isRepeat(...) = true
wheelSteps(0xFF880000) = -1
```
hints: To read bits `a` upwards, shift right by `a`, then keep the width you need with `&`: `0xFFFF` for 16 bits, `0xFF` for 8, `1` for a single bit.
For signed 16-bit values, cast the masked 16 bits to `std::int16_t`: `0xFFFF` becomes -1.
